quote: Skewes (1933) proved that, assuming that the Riemann hypothesis is true, there exists a number x violating π(x) < li(x), below e^(e^(e^79)) < 10^(10^(10^34))
note: Littlewood proved in 1914 that a crossing between π(x) and li(x) must exist, but Skewes made this proof effective in 1933 by computing an actual upper bound. Skewes is credited with introducing the number itself in 1933.
